## Mark up Balmer

*Colonial Office List*, 1936, Record of Services. OCR excerpt, entry `col1936-p832b11`. A source reference lets us return to the page; the OCR is not the page image.

> BALMER, F. E.—Dep. chief acctnt., G.P.O., E. Africa Prot., Mar., 1919; ch. acctnt., G.P.O., Kenya, Oct., 1919; ch. acctnt., Kenya-Uganda-Tanganyika post and tel. service, 1933; senr. dep. P.M.G., do., 1935.

**Three minutes:** underline the last two positions, circle their places and box their years. What does “do.” refer to? How would you record that the place was inherited?

My decision and reason:

_________________________________________________________________________

_________________________________________________________________________

The target is one event per posting: position, place, start and end year, acting status, and whether the place was inherited. Keep the source reference and printed wording alongside the interpretation.

## A second entry for later

*Colonial Office List*, 1889, entry `col1889-p554b20`.

> TRIMEN, HENRY, M.B. (Lond.), F.R.S., F.L.S. —Formerly lecturer on botany at St. Mary's Hospital, London, 1867 to 1875; was senior assistant to department of botany, British Museum, 1869 to 1879; director Royal Botanical Gardens, Ceylon, Feb., 1880; author of numerous works and papers on pure and applied botany.

Two appointments overlap. Should the record preserve both? Is “British Museum” an institution, a location, or both for your research question?

## Three decisions with reasons

Take six minutes. Choose **accept**, **reject**, or **unresolved** for each proposal. Give the evidence that decided it; if unresolved, say what you would check. We will discuss R8 together.

### R1 · Blakely

Source, *Colonial Office List* 1905: “BLAKELY, DONALD QUENTIN.—Clk., atty.-gen.'s off., B. Honduras, Apl., 1898.”

**Proposal:** birth year 1898; one posting, “Clk., atty.-gen.'s officer”, in B. Honduras, with no event year.

The place and position are recognisable, and the model was told to extract only printed facts. But the entry has no birth clause; its date belongs to the appointment. “Off.” means office here.

### R3 · Abery and Carbery

**ABERY, Joseph:** M.B.C.M.; 1867 Ceylon, assistant colonial surgeon; one edition (1897).

**CARBERY, Joseph:** M.B.C.M.; same dated appointment; six editions, including 1897.

**Proposal:** merge the biographies. The forename, qualification and appointment agree, and the shorter surname could be an OCR loss. Against: the surnames differ, and one shared event may need corroboration.

### R8 · Harris

Source, *Colonial Office List* 1927 (OCR excerpt; omissions marked): “HARRIS, SIR CHARLES ALEXANDER ... B. 1858; scholar, prizeman, and Porteus medallist of Christ's Coll., Camb.; ... gov. and c. in c., Newfoundland, 1st Nov., 1917; assumed govt., 17th Dec., 1917; ret., 1922.”

The retrieved Charles Alexander Harris item names Christ’s College and the Newfoundland governorship, but gives birth in **1855**.

**Proposal:** accept the identity link, preserve **1858** as the source reading, record **1855** separately and flag the disagreement.

The name, college and office agree. The dates conflict; the OCR alone cannot tell us whether the discrepancy began in scanning, printing or the external record. The accounts may also share an underlying source.
